report.title: Weather, demand and a fair comparison
report.subtitle: A validated daily dataset, followed by a chronological benchmark against simple alternatives.
findings: 165 absent date/hour slots are identified before daily totals are compared.
Calendar + weather model has the lowest holdout MAE: 680.4 rentals per day.
The weather model trails the seven-day lag in 1 of three earlier validation periods, exposing sensitivity to time period.

series.name: Mean absolute error, lower is better

methodology.title: Quality gate before modelling
methodology.body: Require unique date/hour keys, valid count identities and complete 24-hour coverage. Decode GHCN missing values and reject quality-flagged weather observations before a one-to-one daily join.

methodology.title: Chronological benchmark
methodology.body: Fixed 80/20 chronological split; fixed hyperparameters; no test-set tuning; observed contemporaneous weather; rolling observed seven-day lag. Three expanding-window validation folds stay inside the training period. Calendar-only and calendar-plus-weather models use the same fixed estimator settings. MAE and RMSE are evaluated on the same dates.

methodology.title: Decision boundary
methodology.body: Contemporaneous observed weather makes this retrospective demand estimation, not a production forecast. Missing dates, seasonal changes and system growth affect generalization. A single holdout does not establish future business impact.

report.notes: Input fingerprints and software versions are saved with the report. The NOAA station source is mutable.
